description: EvacTunnel estimates how many people would be trapped, injured or killed, and how long evacuation would take, when an emergency such as a fire, crash or spill occurs inside a road tunnel. It was developed by the GIDAI fire safety research group at the University of Cantabria in Spain and is described in two 2013 journal papers on decision support and real-time stochastic evacuation for road tunnels. The model covers one-way tunnels, and bidirectional tunnels are handled by running it once for each direction. It uses Monte Carlo simulation of vehicles and occupants, and for fires it accounts for smoke moving along the tunnel. Outputs are the number of trapped vehicles by type and the mean, standard deviation and percentiles of trapped, dead and injured persons and of total evacuation time. The program is free: the Windows installation package and a help file are available to download from the GIDAI website. Caveats: it runs only on older Windows versions (2000 to 8.1), no source code or licence text is published, and the package dates from about 2010. Simulation uses: comparing tunnel safety measures and emergency response plans, and estimating casualty ranges for tunnel incident scenarios in emergency service planning. Related records: JuPedSim (model-jupedsim) and the Jülich pedestrian data archive (data-juelich-pedestrian-dynamics-data-archive) support more general evacuation modelling, and CFAST (model-cfast) models smoke in enclosed spaces.
